issues.failure_explanation: With the momentum equation as stated, the added forcing must satisfy \nabla(\tilde p - p) = 10^5 (x_1^{-0.49}, 0)^T, so \tilde p = p + 10^5 x_1^{0.51}/0.51 (up to a constant). The stated correction 10^5 (1.49 x_1^{1.49})^{-1} = 10^5 x_1^{-1.49}/1.49 has x_1-derivative proportional to -x_1^{-2.49}, not x_1^{-0.49}. It is also not integrable near x_1 = 0, so it is not an admissible L^2 pressure. The claimed pressure of the test problem is therefore wrong.

failure_location.quote: only the pressure changes to $\tilde p = p + 10^5 (1.49 \cdot x_1^{1.49})^{-1}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated pressure with \tilde p = p + 10^5 x_1^{0.51}/0.51 (normalized to zero mean if desired), and make sure any reported pressure errors used this correct pressure.
issues.overall_effect: The analytic description of the gradient-field experiment is incorrect, including the pressure that enters the mixed-FEM velocity-error discussion. The velocity solution and the stream-function results are unaffected, since \curl of the added field is zero.
issues.title: Incorrect pressure for the gradient-perturbed numerical test case
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation of the antiderivative fixes the claim. No theorem, rate, or the qualitative pressure-robustness conclusion depends on the wrong formula.
